description:
Whole-universe-invisible fixtures for the narrow-seeded test path
        (SummerTestExtension.builder().beanClasses(...), which indexes the seeds' .class bytes
        directly via NarrowIndexBuilder — the Quarkus ArcTestContainer beanClasses(...) model). Two kinds live here: the intentionally-broken beans for sad-path
        TCK tests (circular dependency, missing dependency, ambiguous resolution, self-injection)
        and the narrow-only positive fixtures that the whole universe must never see (e.g. the
        row-model metadata regression's config, whose stub DataSource would collide with the tck's
        JdbcTestConfig).

        This module deliberately does NOT declare the jandex-maven-plugin, so it
        produces no jandex.idx. The compiled .class files still ship in the jar
        and are on the test classpath (so NarrowIndexBuilder can read them). They
        are invisible to the whole-universe @SummerTest container because that
        container indexes exactly the running test class's OWN test-classes
        directory (Quarkus @QuarkusTest model, via TestClassIndexer) -- a separate
        module's test-classes are simply not on that path. No exclude list is
        needed: the boundary is the (absence of an) archive on the indexed path,
        not an allow/deny pattern.

        The "no jandex.idx" choice is the explicit, defensive half of that
        boundary -- even though the test-classes path already excludes this
        module, producing no index removes any chance of these broken beans
        surfacing as a whole-universe archive. Do NOT add the jandex-maven-plugin
        here: a scanned @Component in this module would be discovered and rejected
        by every normal TCK, not just the sad-path ones.

        Package note: fixtures live under com.github.dropguard.summer.tck.invisible.fixtures.* so the
        package prefix mirrors the module name (summer-tck-invisible-fixtures).
        This keeps "which module owns this fixture" readable from the import
        alone -- the positive fixtures in summer-tck-fixtures use
        com.github.dropguard.summer.tck.fixtures.*, so the two modules no longer share a package
        prefix.
